facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
The applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) took part in the demonstration on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
The applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were arrested at the venue of the demonstration on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
After their arrest, the applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were taken to police stations.
At the police stations, the applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were charged with administrative offences.
The applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were convicted of administrative offences as charged by the justices of the peace.

The administrative offence record stated that the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) conduct was in breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, demonstrating his refusal to obey the lawful orders of the police officers and preventing them from fulfilling their service duties.
On 29 May 2012 the Justice of the Peace of circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow examined the administrative charges against the first applicant (Mr Asainov) in his presence.

On the basis of the statements of two police officers, the Justice of the Peace of circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow established that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had committed an administrative offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, as described in the administrative offence record.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Asainov), as a participant in the authorised demonstration on 6 May 2012, had broken through the police cordon and tried to pass to Red Square.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had ignored the police orders to cease his actions of breaking through the police cordon on 6 May 2012.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had actively resisted the police officers while being taken to the police van on 6 May 2012.
The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had thrown stones, glass bottles and smoke bombs.
The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had disregarded multiple demands by the police to cease his actions.
The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had resisted arrest.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early and began to disperse the participants.
It took the police about two hours to clear the protestors from Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The administrative arrest record for the first applicant (Mr Asainov) indicated that he had been released at 11.05 p.m. on 6 May 2012.
A duty officer at the Fili-Davydkovo district police station drew up an administrative offence record in respect of the first applicant (Mr Asainov).
The appeal decision of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow of 23 August 2012 did not mention the eye-witness statement submitted by the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) wife.

Relying on the testimony of the two police officers, the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow upheld the first-instance judgment convicting the first applicant (Mr Asainov) of an administrative offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
